It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Ahmad ibn Zuhayr related to us: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah al-Hawti related to us: Abu al-Mughirah 'Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, from Artah ibn al-Mundhir [[In (T): "Ibn Jarir related here a strange, wondrous report with its chain."]] who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said to him, while Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman was with him: "Inform me about the interpretation of Allah's words: ﴿Ha, Mim. 'Ayn, Sin, Qaf.﴾" He lowered his head, then turned away from him. Then he repeated his question, and he turned away from him again, giving him no answer and disliking his question. Then he repeated it a third time, and he did not respond to him at all. Then Hudhayfah said [[In (A): "Then Hudhayfah said to him."]]: "I will inform you of it. I know why he disliked it. It was revealed concerning a man of his family called 'Abd al-Ilah' (or 'Abd Allah), who will settle by a river of the rivers of the East, on which two cities will be built, and the river will split between them. When Allah permits the removal of their dominion, the end of their state and their term, Allah will send a fire upon one of them by night, and in the morning it will be black and dark, having burned, as though it had never been in its place. Its companion will wake up amazed: how did it escape? Then there will be only the brightness of that day until every stubborn tyrant among them gathers in it. Then Allah will cause it and them all to sink into the earth. That is His words: ﴿Ha, Mim. 'Ayn, Sin, Qaf.﴾ Meaning: a determination from Allah the Exalted and a trial and a decree. Ha, Mim [[In (T), (M), (A): 'Mudunatayn' (two cities).]]: 'Ha, Mim' means... 'Ayn' means justice from Him, Sin means 'sa-yakun' (it will be), Qaf means it will certainly occur upon these two cities."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/5), and Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated it in al-Fitan, no. (568), through the chain of Abu al-Mughirah from Artah ibn al-Mundhir from one who narrated to him from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned it.]]

Even more strange than this is what the huffaz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili narrated in the second part of the Musnad of Ibn 'Abbas, and from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet ﷺ concerning this. But its chain is extremely weak and broken (munqati'), for he said:

Abu Talib 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn 'Asim related to us: Abu 'Abd al-Malik al-Hasan ibn Yahya al-Khushani al-Dimashqi related to us, from Abu Mu'awiyah, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab ascended the pulpit and said: "O people, has any one of you heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explain ﴿Ha, Mim. 'Ayn, Sin, Qaf﴾?" Ibn 'Abbas leapt up and said: "I have." He said: "'Ha, Mim' is one of the names of Allah the Exalted." He said: "Then 'Ayn?" He said: "The ones who turned away witnessed the punishment of the Day of Badr." He said: "Then Sin?" He said: "﴿Those who have done wrong will know to what return they will be returned.﴾" He said: "Then Qaf?" He was silent. Then Abu Dharr stood up and explained it as Ibn 'Abbas had said, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said: "Qaf: a calamity from the sky that will overwhelm the people."[[Ibn 'Asakir narrated it in his History, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/336).]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thus does He reveal to you and to those before you, Allah, the Almighty, the Wise﴾, meaning: just as He revealed this Qur'an to you, so He revealed the Books and the Scrolls to the prophets before you. His words ﴿Allah, the Almighty﴾ mean: in His retribution; ﴿the Wise﴾ means: in His sayings and His actions.

Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, related from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah: that al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, how does the revelation come to you?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and it is the hardest on me, then it departs from me, and I have retained what it said. And sometimes the angel appears to me in the form of a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says." 'A'ishah said: "I saw him when revelation came down upon him on a very cold day, and it would depart from him, and his forehead would be dripping with sweat."

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs, and the wording is that of al-Bukhari.[[Muwatta' (1/202), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2), and Sahih Muslim no. (2333).]]

It was also related by al-Tabarani from 'Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad, from his father, from 'Amir ibn Salih, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, from al-Harith ibn Hisham: that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "How does the revelation descend upon you?" He said: "Like the ringing of a bell, and it departs from me, and I have retained what it said." He said: "And it is the hardest on me." He said: "And sometimes the angel comes to me, takes the form of a man for me, speaks to me, and I retain what he says."[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/259).]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Amr ibn al-Walid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, do you perceive the revelation?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I hear sounds of ringing, then I fall silent at that point. Every time revelation comes to me, I think my soul is being taken." Ahmad alone narrated it.[[Al-Musnad (2/222).]]

We have already mentioned the manner in which revelation comes to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the beginning of the explanation of al-Bukhari, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated here. To Allah belongs all praise and grace.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning: all are servants of Him and possessions of His, under His subjugation and control. ﴿And He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾, like His saying: ﴿the Great, the Exalted﴾ [al-Ra'd: 9] and ﴿And He is the Most High, the Great﴾ [Saba': 23]. The verses on this are many.

* *

His saying: ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart from above them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Ka'b al-Ahbar said: meaning, out of fear, from the greatness [of Allah]. ﴿And the angels exalt the praise of their Lord and seek forgiveness for those on the earth﴾, like His saying: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it exalt the praise of their Lord and believe in Him and seek forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge"﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

* *

His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ is an announcement of this and an emphasis upon it.

* *

His saying: ﴿And those who have taken protectors other than Him﴾ means the polytheists. ﴿Allah is Watchful over them﴾, meaning: Witness over their deeds, counting them and enumerating them, and He will recompense them with the fullest recompense. ﴿And you are not over them a guardian﴾, meaning: you are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer of all things.

* *

His saying: "there is no doubt about it" — that is, there is no doubt about its occurrence, and that it will certainly happen. His saying: "a party will be in the Garden and a party in the Blaze" is like His saying: "The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering — that is the Day of Mutual Loss (al-taghabun)" [al-Taghabun: 9], meaning the people of Paradise will defraud the people of the Fire. And like His saying, the Exalted: "That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed. And We do not delay it except for a term already counted. On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission; among them will be wretched and happy" [Hud: 103–105].

Imam Ahmad narrated: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Abu Qabil al-Ma'afiri narrated to me, from Shufayy al-Asbahi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us holding two books in his hand, and said: "Do you know what these two books are?" We said: "No, unless you inform us, O Messenger of Allah." He said to the one in his right hand: "This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, with the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and their tribes, then the list is closed upon the last of them — none will be added to them nor subtracted from them, ever." Then he said to the one in his left hand: "This is the book of the people of the Fire, with their names, the names of their fathers and their tribes, then the list is closed upon the last of them — none will be added to them nor subtracted from them, ever." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then for what do we work, if this is a matter already decided?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be upright and close to the mark, for the companion of Paradise is concluded with the deeds of the people of Paradise, however he may have acted; and the companion of the Fire is concluded with the deeds of the people of the Fire, however he may have acted." Then he gestured with his hand, closed it, and said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has finished with the servants." Then he said, with his right hand, casting it away, "A party in the Garden," and cast away with his left, saying, "A party in the Blaze."

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed us that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Adi ibn al-Hamra' al-Zuhri informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say — while he was standing at al-Hazwara in the market of Makkah: "By Allah, you are the best of Allah's lands and the most beloved of Allah's lands to Allah, and had I not been expelled from you, I would not have left."

The same report is narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through al-Zuhri with the same chain. al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and sound).

* *

His saying: "and warn of the Day of Gathering" — which is the Day of Resurrection, when Allah will gather the first and the last on one plain.

* *

His saying: "there is no doubt about it" — that is, there is no doubt about its occurrence, and that it will certainly happen. His saying: "a party will be in the Garden and a party in the Blaze" is like His saying: "The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering — that is the Day of Mutual Loss (al-taghabun)" [al-Taghabun: 9], meaning the people of Paradise will defraud the people of the Fire. And like His saying, the Exalted: "That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed. And We do not delay it except for a term already counted. On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission; among them will be wretched and happy" [Hud: 103–105].

Imam Ahmad narrated: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Abu Qabil al-Ma'afiri narrated to me, from Shufayy al-Asbahi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us holding two books in his hand, and said: "Do you know what these two books are?" We said: "No, unless you inform us, O Messenger of Allah." He said to the one in his right hand: "This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, with the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and their tribes, then the list is closed upon the last of them — none will be added to them nor subtracted from them, ever." Then he said to the one in his left hand: "This is the book of the people of the Fire, with their names, the names of their fathers and their tribes, then the list is closed upon the last of them — none will be added to them nor subtracted from them, ever." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then for what do we work, if this is a matter already decided?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be upright and close to the mark, for the companion of Paradise is concluded with the deeds of the people of Paradise, however he may have acted; and the companion of the Fire is concluded with the deeds of the people of the Fire, however he may have acted." Then he gestured with his hand, closed it, and said: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has finished with the servants." Then he said, with his right hand, casting it away, "A party in the Garden," and cast away with his left, saying, "A party in the Blaze."

This was narrated likewise by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i together, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Bakr ibn Mudar, both from Abu Qabil, from Shufayy ibn Mati' al-Asbahi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, with the same wording.

al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib."

al-Baghawi also cited it in his tafsir through the route of Bishr ibn Bakr, from Sa'id ibn 'Uthman, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning it in similar form. In his version there are additions, among them: "Then he said: 'A party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze, a justice from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Salih (scribe of al-Layth), from al-Layth, with the same.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Abu Qabil, from Shufayy, from a man among the Companions, and he mentioned it.

Then it is also related from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith and Haywah ibn Shurayh, from Yahya ibn Abi Usayd, that Abu Firas narrated to him that he heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr say: "When Allah created Adam, He shook him as one shakes a provision pouch, and brought out from him all his offspring. They came out like specks of dust. He grasped them in two handfuls and said: 'A wretched one and a happy one.' Then He threw them, then grasped them again and said: 'A party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze.'"

This stopped report (mawquf) is closer to the correct, and Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Hammad — meaning Ibn Salamah — narrated to us, al-Jurayri informed us, from Abu Nadrah, that a man from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), called Abu 'Abd Allah, whose companions came in to visit him while he was weeping. They said to him: "What makes you weep? Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not tell you: 'Trim your moustache, then leave it until you meet me'?" He said: "Yes, but I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed Allah grasped with His right hand a handful, and another with the other hand, and said: These are for this, and these are for this, and I do not mind.' So I do not know in which of the two handfuls I am."

The narrations about predestination (qadar) in the Sahihs, Sunans and Musnads are very numerous, among them the hadith of 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, 'A'ishah, and a great many others.

His saying: "Had Allah willed, He would have made them one community" — that is, either upon guidance or upon misguidance. But He differentiated among them: He guides whom He wills to the truth, and leaves astray whom He wills from it, and to Him belong wisdom and the conclusive proof. Hence He said: "But He admits whom He wills into His mercy; and the wrongdoers — they have no protector nor helper" [al-Shura: 8].

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu Suwayd, who narrated to him from Ibn Hujayrah: that it reached him that Musa, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, Your creatures whom You created — You made from them a party in Paradise and a party in the Fire. Would it not be better if You had admitted them all into Paradise?" He said: "O Musa, raise your cubit." He raised it. He said: "I have raised it." He said: "Raise it." He raised it, and left nothing. He said: "O Lord, I have raised it." He said: "Raise it." He said: "I have raised it, except what has no good in it." He said: "Thus I shall admit all My creatures into Paradise, except what has no good in it."

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says, rebuking the polytheists for taking deities besides Allah, and informing that He is the true Protector (al-Wali al-Haqq), to whom alone worship is due, for He is the One able to give life to the dead, and He is over all things Powerful.

Then He said: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its judgment is with Allah﴾, meaning: whatever matters you differ over; this is general for all things. ﴿Its judgment is with Allah﴾, meaning: He is the Judge concerning it by His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ, as in His saying: ﴿And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa: 59].

﴿That is Allah, my Lord﴾, meaning: the Judge in all things. ﴿Upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn back﴾, meaning: I return to Him in all matters.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Creator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: Their Creator and that which is between them. ﴿He made for you spouses from yourselves﴾, meaning: of your own kind and form, as a favour and bounty upon you; He made from your own kind males and females. ﴿And of the cattle, pairs﴾, meaning: He created for you eight pairs of cattle.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾, meaning: He creates you through it, i.e., through that creation in this manner; He continually multiplies you therein, males and females, creation after creation, generation after generation, offspring after offspring, among humankind and the cattle.

Al-Baghawi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾ means in the womb. It was also said: in the belly. It was also said: in this form of creation.

Mujahid said: "And offspring after offspring, among humankind and the cattle."

It was also said: "fi" (in) carries the meaning of "ba'" (with), i.e., He multiplies you by it.

﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾, meaning: nothing is like the Creator of all pairs; for He is the One, the Eternal Refuge (As-Samad), who has no equal. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾.

Allah, exalted is He, says to this Ummah: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you (O Muhammad)﴾. He mentions the first of the Messengers after Adam, who is Noah, peace be upon him, and the last of them, who is Muhammad (ﷺ). Then He mentions, from among them, the Ulul-'Azm (the Messengers of firm resolve), who are Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses) and 'Isa (Jesus), the son of Maryam (Mary), peace be upon them. This verse comprises the mention of the five, just as the verse of al-Ahzab includes them in His saying: ﴿And when We took from the Prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, and Ibrahim, and Musa, and 'Isa, the son of Maryam﴾ [al-Ahzab: 7], and so on. The religion that all the Messengers brought is: the worship of Allah alone, with no partner, as He said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. And in the hadith: "We, the company of the Prophets, are paternal half-brothers (awlad 'allat); our religion is one." That is, the common element among them is the worship of Allah alone, with no partner, even though their laws (shara'i') and methods (manahij) differ, as in His saying: ﴿For each of you We have made a law (shir'ah) and a method (minhaj)﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48]. Therefore He said here: ﴿that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾, meaning: Allah, exalted is He, enjoined upon all the Prophets, peace be upon them, unity and community, and forbade them from division and disagreement.

* *

His saying: ﴿Hard upon the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾ means: it was difficult for them, and they denied what you call them to, O Muhammad, of monotheism.

Then He said: ﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back (in repentance)﴾. That is: it is He who decrees guidance for whoever deserves it, and who ordains misguidance upon whoever prefers it over the path of right guidance. Therefore He said: ﴿And they did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them﴾. That is: their opposition to the truth occurred only after it had reached them and the proof had been established against them, and nothing drove them to that except rebellion (al-baghy), obstinacy (al-'inad) and hostility (al-mushaqqah).

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And were it not for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term﴾. That is: were it not for the word that preceded from Allah to grant respite to the servants until the reckoning of them on the Day of Return, He would have hastened punishment for them swiftly in this world.

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them﴾ refers to the later generation after the first generation, who denied the truth, ﴿are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾. That is: they are not certain of their affair; rather they are imitators (muqallidun) of their fathers and forefathers, without evidence or proof, and they are in confusion about their affair, in disquieting doubt, and in far-reaching dissension.

This verse contains ten independent clauses, each separate from the one before it, and each with a ruling of its own. They said: there is no parallel to it except the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), for it also has ten such divisions.

His words, ﴿So for that, invite [them]﴾, mean: for the religion which We revealed to you, the religion We enjoined upon all the messengers before you, the bearers of the great laws who are followed, such as the Resolute Messengers (Ulu al-'Azm) and others, so invite the people to it.

* *

His words, ﴿and remain steadfast as you have been commanded﴾, mean: remain steadfast, you and those who follow you, in the worship of Allah, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you.

* *

His words, ﴿and do not follow their desires﴾, refer to the polytheists in what they invented, denied, and fabricated of the worship of idols.

* *

His words, ﴿and say: I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down﴾, mean: I affirm all the Books sent down from heaven upon the prophets, and we do not differentiate between any one of them.

* *

His words, ﴿and I have been commanded to be just among you﴾, mean: in judgment, as Allah has commanded me.

* *

His words, ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord﴾, mean: He is the one worshipped, there is no god besides Him. We acknowledge this by choice, and you, even if you do not do so by choice, yet to Him prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly.

* *

His words, ﴿For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds﴾, mean: we are free of you, as the Exalted said: ﴿And if they deny you, say: For me is my deed, and for you is your deed. You are free from what I do, and I am free from what you do﴾ [Yunus 10:41].

* *

His words, ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾: Mujahid said: that is, there is no dispute. As-Suddi said: this was before the revelation of the Verse of the Sword (Ayat al-Sayf). This is well-founded, because this verse is Meccan, and the Verse of the Sword came after the Hijrah.

* *

His words, ﴿Allah will gather us together﴾, mean: on the Day of Resurrection, as in His saying: ﴿Say: Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us with truth, and He is the Judge, the All-Knowing﴾ [Saba' 34:26].

* *

His words, ﴿and to Him is the final return﴾, mean: the place of return and resort on the Day of Reckoning.

Allah, exalted is He, says, threatening those who turn people away from the path of Allah and from those who believe in Him: ﴿And those who dispute concerning Allah after He has been responded to﴾, i.e., they argue with the believers who have responded to Allah and His Messenger, in order to turn them away from the guidance they have adopted. ﴿Their argument is invalid with their Lord﴾, i.e., it is false before Allah. ﴿And upon them is wrath﴾, i.e., from Him. ﴿And for them is a severe punishment﴾, i.e., on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: They argued with the believers after the believers had responded to Allah and His Messenger, in order to turn them away from guidance, and they hoped that the state of Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance) would return.

Qatadah said: They are the Jews and the Christians, who said to the believers: "Our religion is better than your religion, and our prophet came before your prophet, and we are better than you and more entitled to Allah than you." But they lied in this.

Then He said: ﴿Allah is the One who has sent down the Book with truth﴾, meaning the Books sent down from Him upon His prophets, ﴿and the Balance﴾, which is justice and fairness; this was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. This is like His saying: ﴿We had already sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Book and the Balance so that mankind may uphold justice﴾ [al-Hadid: 25], and His saying: ﴿And the sky He raised high and set up the balance. That you not transgress within the balance. And establish weight with justice and do not make the balance deficient﴾ [ar-Rahman: 7-9].

* *

His saying: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ contains encouragement toward it, warning from it, and discouragement from the world.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾, i.e., they say: ﴿When is this promise, if you are truthful?﴾ [Saba: 29]. They say this only out of denial, disbelief, unlikelihood, obstinacy and defiance. ﴿But those who believe are fearful of it﴾, i.e., they are apprehensive and anxious lest it occur, ﴿and they know that it is the truth﴾, i.e., that it will certainly come to pass. So they prepare for it and act for its sake.

It has been related through chains that reach the level of tawatur (mass transmission), in the Sahih and Hasan collections, the Sunan and the Masanid, and in some of its wordings, that a man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a loud voice while he was on some journey; he called out to him saying: "O Muhammad!" Therefore He said: ﴿And if not for a decisive word, it would have been decided between them﴾, meaning they would have been hastened to punishment, were it not for the respite that had preceded until the Day of Return. ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment﴾, meaning a severe, agonizing punishment in Hell, ﴿and wretched is the destination.﴾

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned﴾, meaning in the plains of the Resurrection, ﴿while it is going to befall them﴾, meaning what they fear will certainly befall them without doubt. This is their condition on the day of their return, and they are in this fear and dread. ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise; they will have whatever they wish with their Lord.﴾ How far is this from that! How far is one who is in the plains, in humiliation, disgrace and certain fear because of his wrongdoing, from one who is in the gardens of Paradise, having whatever he wishes of food, drink, clothing, dwellings, sights, spouses and pleasures, of which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has occurred to the heart of a human being.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Abbar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Ansari narrated to us, from Abu Tayyibah, who said: Indeed, the people of Paradise will have a cloud that shades them, and it will say: "What shall I rain upon you?" He said: So no one among the people makes a supplication for anything except that it rains it upon them, until the one who speaks among them says: "Rain upon us maidens of equal age."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, with this chain.

Therefore He said: ﴿That is the great bounty﴾, meaning the great success, the complete and all-encompassing, widespread and general blessing.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 42, verses 23–24 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says, after mentioning the gardens of Paradise for His servants who believed and did righteous deeds: ﴿That is what Allah gives good news of to His servants who believed and did righteous deeds.﴾ That is, this (reward) is certain to be theirs without doubt, by Allah's giving them glad tidings of it.
* *
His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the near of kin.﴾ That is, say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among the disbelievers of Quraysh: I do not ask you for any reward for this delivering of the message and this counsel to you that you would give me. I only ask of you that you restrain your evil from me and leave me to convey the messages of my Lord. If you will not help me, then do not harm me because of the kinship that is between me and you.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, who said: I heard Tawus (report) from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about His saying, the Exalted: ﴿except love for the near of kin﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: (it means) the near of kin of Muhammad's family. Ibn 'Abbas said: You have been hasty. The Prophet ﷺ had no clan of Quraysh except that he had kinship among them. So he said: "except that you maintain the ties of kinship that are between me and you." Al-Bukhari alone reported it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4818, and al-Musnad (1/229).]

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Yahya al-Qattan, from Shu'bah, with it. Similarly, 'Amir al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, al-'Awfi, Yusuf ibn Mihran and others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas the like of it. And Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Abu Malik, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others said the same.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Yazid al-Tabarani and Ja'far al-Qalanisi narrated to us, both saying: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "I do not ask you for any reward for it, except that you love me for my kinship with you, and that you protect the kinship that is between me and you." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/435).]

Imam Ahmad also narrated from Hasan ibn Musa: Qaza'ah, meaning Ibn Suwayd, narrated to us — and Ibn Abi Hatim — from his father, from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Qaza'ah ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I do not ask you for any reward for what I have brought you of clear proofs and guidance, except that you love Allah and draw near to Him through obedience to Him." [Al-Musnad (1/268).]

Similarly, Qatadah narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri the like of it.

This appears to be an interpretation according to a second opinion: it is as if he means ﴿except love for the near of kin﴾ — that is, except that you act in obedience that brings you near to Allah in closeness.

A third opinion, which al-Bukhari and others related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the meaning of which is that he said: the meaning of that is that you love me for my kinship, that is, that you treat them well and be kind to them.

Al-Suddi said, from Abu al-Daylam: When 'Ali ibn al-Husayn was brought as a captive and stood on the steps of Damascus, a man from the people of Syria stood and said: "Praise be to Allah who killed you, uprooted you, and cut off the two horns of strife." 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said to him: "Have you read the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you read Ha Mim?" He said: "I have read the Qur'an, but I have not read Ha Mim." He said: "Have you not read: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the near of kin﴾?" He said: "And are you they?" He said: "Yes."

Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i said: I asked 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb about His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the near of kin﴾, and he said: "The near of kin of the Prophet ﷺ." Ibn Jarir related both of these. [Tafsir al-Tabari (25/17).]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, 'Abd al-Salam narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to me, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Ansar said: "We did this and we did that," as if they were boasting. Ibn 'Abbas — or al-'Abbas, 'Abd al-Salam was uncertain — said: "We have the virtue over you." This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he came to them in their gatherings and said: "O assembly of the Ansar, were you not humble, and did Allah not give you might through me?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Were you not misguided, and did Allah not guide you through me?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Will you not answer me?" They said: "What should we say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Will you not say: 'Did your people not drive you out, and did we not shelter you? Or did they not deny you, and did we not believe you? Or did they not forsake you, and did we not help you?'" He kept saying this until they knelt on their knees and said: "Our wealth and what is in our hands belongs to Allah and His Messenger." He said: Then this was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the near of kin.﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari (25/16).]

Ibn Abi Hatim similarly narrated it from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from 'Abd al-Mu'min ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd al-Salam, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad — and he is weak — with his chain, the like of it or close to it.

In the two Sahihs, in the section on the spoils of Hunayn, there is something close to this context, but it does not mention the revelation of this verse. The mention of its revelation in Medina is problematic, because the surah is Meccan, and there is no clear connection between this noble verse and the context.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, a man whom he named narrated to us, Husayn al-Ashqar narrated to us, from Qays, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the near of kin﴾, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are these whose love Allah has commanded?" He said: "Fatimah and her sons, peace be upon them." [Al-Tabarani also narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/444), by way of Harb al-Tahhan from Husayn al-Ashqar with it.]

This chain is weak. It contains an unidentified, unknown narrator, from a Shi'i shaykh who is unreliable, namely Husayn al-Ashqar, and his report cannot be accepted in this context. The mention of this verse's revelation in Medina is also far-fetched, for the verse is Meccan, and at that time Fatimah had no children at all, since she did not marry 'Ali until after Badr, in the second year after the Hijrah.

The truth is to interpret the verse as the Imam, the scholar of the Ummah and interpreter of the Qur'an, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas interpreted it, as al-Bukhari related from him [may Allah have mercy on him]. Love for the Ahl al-Bayt (the family of the Prophet), enjoining good towards them, and honouring and respecting them, is not to be denied, for they are from a pure lineage, from the most noble house that has existed on the face of the earth, in glory, lineage and descent. This is especially so when they follow the clear, manifest and evident Prophetic Sunnah, as their predecessors did, such as al-'Abbas and his sons, and 'Ali and his household and descendants, may Allah be pleased with them all.

It is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in his sermon at Ghadir Khumm: "I am leaving among you the two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my family (ʿitrah), and they will not part from each other until they come to me at the Pool." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2408, in similar wording, from the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam.]

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, when some of Quraysh meet others, they greet them with a good cheerful face, but when they meet us, they greet us with faces we do not recognise?" He said: The Prophet ﷺ became very angry, and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, faith does not enter a man's heart until he loves you for the sake of Allah and His Messenger." [Al-Musnad (1/207).]

Then Ahmad said: Jarir narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Rabi'ah, who said: al-'Abbas entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We go out and see Quraysh talking, and when they see us they fall silent." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry, and a vein between his eyes throbbed. Then he said: "By Allah, faith does not enter the heart of a man until he loves you for the sake of Allah and for my kinship." [Al-Musnad (1/207).]

Al-Bukhari said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Khalid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Waqid, who said: I heard my father narrate from Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Watch over Muhammad ﷺ in his family." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3713.]

In the Sahih: al-Siddiq said to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both: "By Allah, the kinship of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is dearer to me than my own kinship that I maintain." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3712.]

'Umar ibn al-Khattab said to al-'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "By Allah, your Islam on the day you embraced Islam was dearer to me than the Islam of al-Khattab would have been had he embraced it, because your Islam was dearer to the Messenger of Allah than the Islam of al-Khattab."

Thus the condition of the two Shaykhs, may Allah be pleased with them both, is what is obligatory upon everyone to be; and for this reason they were the most virtuous of believers after the Prophets and Messengers, may Allah be pleased with them both and with all the Companions.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, who said: Yazid ibn Hayyan narrated to me: I set out with Husayn ibn Maysarah and 'Umar ibn Muslim to Zayd ibn Arqam. When we sat down with him, Husayn said to him: "You have obtained much good, O Zayd. You saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, you heard his speech, you fought alongside him, and you prayed behind him. You have indeed obtained much good, O Zayd. Narrate to us what you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "O my nephew, by Allah, my age has grown old, my time has passed, and I have forgotten some of what I used to remember from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So accept what I narrate to you, and do not burden me with what I cannot." Then he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once stood among us as an orator at a pond called Khumm, between Mecca and Medina. He praised Allah and extolled Him, and reminded and admonished, then said: 'To proceed: O people, I am only a human being; the messenger of my Lord is about to come to me and I will answer him. I am leaving among you two weighty things. The first of them is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light. So take hold of the Book of Allah and hold fast to it.'" He urged them towards the Book of Allah and encouraged them to it, then said: "And my family (Ahl al-Bayt). I remind you of Allah concerning my family, I remind you of Allah concerning my family, I remind you of Allah concerning my family." Husayn said to him: "And who are his family, O Zayd? Are not his wives from his family?" He said: "His wives are from his family, but his family are those for whom charity is forbidden after him." He said: "And who are they?" He said: "They are the family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of al-'Abbas." He said: "Is charity forbidden for all of these?" He said: "Yes."

Muslim and al-Nasa'i also narrated it in this way from several chains, from Yazid ibn Hayyan. [Al-Musnad (4/366); Sahih Muslim, no. 2408; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 8175.]

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Ali ibn al-Mundhir al-Kufi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id (and al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Zayd ibn Arqam), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am leaving among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after me. One of them is greater than the other: the Book of Allah, a rope extended from the heaven to the earth, and the other is my family (*'itrah*), the people of my household. They will not separate until they come to me at the Basin (*al-Hawd*). So look how you will treat them after me."

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated it. Then he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith.

Al-Tirmidhi also said: Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his pilgrimage, on the Day of 'Arafah, while he was on his she-camel al-Qaswa', delivering a sermon. I heard him say: "O people, I have left among you that which, if you take hold of it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah, and my family (*'itrah*), the people of my household."

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated it, and said: hasan gharib. There are also reports on this subject from Abu Dharr, Abu Sa'id, Zayd ibn Arqam, and Hudhayfah ibn Usayd.

Then al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ma'in narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Nawfali, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, from his father, from his grandfather 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Love Allah for the blessings He nourishes you with, love me for the love of Allah, and love my family for my love."

Then he said: hasan gharib; we only know it through this chain.

We have already cited other hadiths on this subject under His saying, ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you completely﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33] (see the commentary on verse 33 of Surah al-Ahzab), so there is no need to repeat them here. To Allah belong praise and grace.

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Mufaddal ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Hanash, who said: I heard Abu Dharr, while he was holding the ring of the door, saying: "O people, whoever knows me knows me, and whoever does not know me, I am Abu Dharr. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The likeness of my family among you is like the likeness of the ark of Noah: whoever boards it is saved, and whoever stays behind from it is destroyed.'" [Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak and declared it sahih (3/150) through the route of Mufaddal ibn Salih from Abu Ishaq with this chain, and al-Dhahabi criticised it, saying: "Mufaddal ibn Salih is weak (*wahin*)." Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/37) through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Dahir from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Quddus, from al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, and in its chain is 'Abd Allah ibn Dahir al-Razi, who is abandoned (*matruk*).]

This chain is weak.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And whoever earns a good deed, We will increase for him therein goodness﴾, meaning: whoever does a good deed, ﴿We will increase for him therein goodness﴾, meaning: reward and recompense. This is like His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa': 40].

Some of the early generations (*al-salaf*) said: Among the rewards of a good deed is the good deed that follows it, and among the recompense for a bad deed is the bad deed that follows it.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Grateful﴾, meaning: He forgives many bad deeds and multiplies the few good deeds. He conceals and forgives, and He multiplies and is grateful.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented about Allah a lie"? So if Allah willed, He would seal over your heart﴾, meaning: if you had invented a lie against Him, as these ignorant people claim, ﴿He would seal over your heart﴾, meaning: He would have sealed your heart and taken away from you the Qur'an that He had given you. This is like His saying, ﴿And if he had made up about Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and none of you could have held Us off from him﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44–47], meaning: We would have punished him with the most severe punishment, and no one among the people could have prevented that from him.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And Allah will efface falsehood﴾, it is not a conjunction with His saying, ﴿He would seal﴾, which would make it jussive (*majzum*). Rather, it is in the nominative (*marfu'*) as a new sentence (*'ala al-ibtida'*). This was stated by Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), who said: The letter "waw" was omitted in the orthography of the Imam Mushaf (the standard codex), just as it was omitted in His saying, ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [al-'Alaq: 18], and His saying, ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good﴾ [al-Isra': 11].

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And establishes the truth by His words﴾, it is conjoined to ﴿And Allah will efface falsehood and establish the truth﴾, meaning: He makes it real, confirms it, clarifies it, and makes it evident by His words, that is, by His proofs and evidences. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: of what hearts conceal and what secrets hide.

He said: "Fatimah and her sons, peace be upon them." [Al-Tabarani also narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/444), by way of Harb al-Tahhan from Husayn al-Ashqar with it.]

This chain is weak. It contains an unidentified, unknown narrator, from a Shi'i shaykh who is unreliable, namely Husayn al-Ashqar, and his report cannot be accepted in this context. The mention of this verse's revelation in Medina is also far-fetched, for the verse is Meccan, and at that time Fatimah had no children at all, since she did not marry 'Ali until after Badr, in the second year after the Hijrah.

The truth is to interpret the verse as the Imam, the scholar of the Ummah and interpreter of the Qur'an, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas interpreted it, as al-Bukhari related from him [may Allah have mercy on him]. Love for the Ahl al-Bayt (the family of the Prophet), enjoining good towards them, and honouring and respecting them, is not to be denied, for they are from a pure lineage, from the most noble house that has existed on the face of the earth, in glory, lineage and descent. This is especially so when they follow the clear, manifest and evident Prophetic Sunnah, as their predecessors did, such as al-'Abbas and his sons, and 'Ali and his household and descendants, may Allah be pleased with them all.

It is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in his sermon at Ghadir Khumm: "I am leaving among you the two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my family (ʿitrah), and they will not part from each other until they come to me at the Pool." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2408, in similar wording, from the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam.]

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, when some of Quraysh meet others, they greet them with a good cheerful face, but when they meet us, they greet us with faces we do not recognise?" He said: The Prophet ﷺ became very angry, and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, faith does not enter a man's heart until he loves you for the sake of Allah and His Messenger." [Al-Musnad (1/207).]

Then Ahmad said: Jarir narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Rabi'ah, who said: al-'Abbas entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We go out and see Quraysh talking, and when they see us they fall silent." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry, and a vein between his eyes throbbed. Then he said: "By Allah, faith does not enter the heart of a man until he loves you for the sake of Allah and for my kinship." [Al-Musnad (1/207).]

Al-Bukhari said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Khalid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Waqid, who said: I heard my father narrate from Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Watch over Muhammad ﷺ in his family." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3713.]

In the Sahih: al-Siddiq said to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both: "By Allah, the kinship of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is dearer to me than my own kinship that I maintain." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3712.]

'Umar ibn al-Khattab said to al-'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "By Allah, your Islam on the day you embraced Islam was dearer to me than the Islam of al-Khattab would have been had he embraced it, because your Islam was dearer to the Messenger of Allah than the Islam of al-Khattab."

Thus the condition of the two Shaykhs, may Allah be pleased with them both, is what is obligatory upon everyone to be; and for this reason they were the most virtuous of believers after the Prophets and Messengers, may Allah be pleased with them both and with all the Companions.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, who said: Yazid ibn Hayyan narrated to me: I set out with Husayn ibn Maysarah and 'Umar ibn Muslim to Zayd ibn Arqam. When we sat down with him, Husayn said to him: "You have obtained much good, O Zayd. You saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, you heard his speech, you fought alongside him, and you prayed behind him. You have indeed obtained much good, O Zayd. Narrate to us what you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "O my nephew, by Allah, my age has grown old, my time has passed, and I have forgotten some of what I used to remember from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So accept what I narrate to you, and do not burden me with what I cannot." Then he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once stood among us as an orator at a pond called Khumm, between Mecca and Medina. He praised Allah and extolled Him, and reminded and admonished, then said: 'To proceed: O people, I am only a human being; the messenger of my Lord is about to come to me and I will answer him. I am leaving among you two weighty things. The first of them is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light. So take hold of the Book of Allah and hold fast to it.'" He urged them towards the Book of Allah and encouraged them to it, then said: "And my family (Ahl al-Bayt). I remind you of Allah concerning my family, I remind you of Allah concerning my family, I remind you of Allah concerning my family." Husayn said to him: "And who are his family, O Zayd? Are not his wives from his family?" He said: "His wives are from his family, but his family are those for whom charity is forbidden after him." He said: "And who are they?" He said: "They are the family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of al-'Abbas." He said: "Is charity forbidden for all of these?" He said: "Yes."

Muslim and al-Nasa'i also narrated it in this way from several chains, from Yazid ibn Hayyan. [Al-Musnad (4/366); Sahih Muslim, no. 2408; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 8175.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 42, verses 23–24 (part 2 of 2):

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Ali ibn al-Mundhir al-Kufi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id (and al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Zayd ibn Arqam), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am leaving among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after me. One of them is greater than the other: the Book of Allah, a rope extended from the heaven to the earth, and the other is my family (*'itrah*), the people of my household. They will not separate until they come to me at the Basin (*al-Hawd*). So look how you will treat them after me."

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated it. Then he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith.

Al-Tirmidhi also said: Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his pilgrimage, on the Day of 'Arafah, while he was on his she-camel al-Qaswa', delivering a sermon. I heard him say: "O people, I have left among you that which, if you take hold of it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah, and my family (*'itrah*), the people of my household."

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated it, and said: hasan gharib. There are also reports on this subject from Abu Dharr, Abu Sa'id, Zayd ibn Arqam, and Hudhayfah ibn Usayd.

Then al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ma'in narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Nawfali, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, from his father, from his grandfather 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Love Allah for the blessings He nourishes you with, love me for the love of Allah, and love my family for my love."

Then he said: hasan gharib; we only know it through this chain.

We have already cited other hadiths on this subject under His saying, ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you completely﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33] (see the commentary on verse 33 of Surah al-Ahzab), so there is no need to repeat them here. To Allah belong praise and grace.

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Mufaddal ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Hanash, who said: I heard Abu Dharr, while he was holding the ring of the door, saying: "O people, whoever knows me knows me, and whoever does not know me, I am Abu Dharr. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The likeness of my family among you is like the likeness of the ark of Noah: whoever boards it is saved, and whoever stays behind from it is destroyed.'" [Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak and declared it sahih (3/150) through the route of Mufaddal ibn Salih from Abu Ishaq with this chain, and al-Dhahabi criticised it, saying: "Mufaddal ibn Salih is weak (*wahin*)." Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/37) through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Dahir from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Quddus, from al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, and in its chain is 'Abd Allah ibn Dahir al-Razi, who is abandoned (*matruk*).]

This chain is weak.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And whoever earns a good deed, We will increase for him therein goodness﴾, meaning: whoever does a good deed, ﴿We will increase for him therein goodness﴾, meaning: reward and recompense. This is like His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa': 40].

Some of the early generations (*al-salaf*) said: Among the rewards of a good deed is the good deed that follows it, and among the recompense for a bad deed is the bad deed that follows it.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Grateful﴾, meaning: He forgives many bad deeds and multiplies the few good deeds. He conceals and forgives, and He multiplies and is grateful.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented about Allah a lie"? So if Allah willed, He would seal over your heart﴾, meaning: if you had invented a lie against Him, as these ignorant people claim, ﴿He would seal over your heart﴾, meaning: He would have sealed your heart and taken away from you the Qur'an that He had given you. This is like His saying, ﴿And if he had made up about Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and none of you could have held Us off from him﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44–47], meaning: We would have punished him with the most severe punishment, and no one among the people could have prevented that from him.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And Allah will efface falsehood﴾, it is not a conjunction with His saying, ﴿He would seal﴾, which would make it jussive (*majzum*). Rather, it is in the nominative (*marfu'*) as a new sentence (*'ala al-ibtida'*). This was stated by Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), who said: The letter "waw" was omitted in the orthography of the Imam Mushaf (the standard codex), just as it was omitted in His saying, ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [al-'Alaq: 18], and His saying, ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good﴾ [al-Isra': 11].

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And establishes the truth by His words﴾, it is conjoined to ﴿And Allah will efface falsehood and establish the truth﴾, meaning: He makes it real, confirms it, clarifies it, and makes it evident by His words, that is, by His proofs and evidences. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: of what hearts conceal and what secrets hide.

Allah the Exalted says, bestowing favour upon His servants by accepting their repentance to Him when they repent and turn back to Him. It is part of His generosity and forbearance that He pardons, overlooks, conceals and forgives, as in His saying: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks Allah's forgiveness will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [an-Nisa': 110]. It is established in Sahih Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, where he said: Muhammad ibn as-Sabbah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, [[In manuscript A: "qalaa" (both said).]] saying: Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah narrated to us, saying: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, and he was his paternal uncle [[In manuscript T: "his uncle, may Allah be pleased with him."]], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more delighted at the repentance of His servant when he turns to Him than any one of you who has his riding beast in a barren desert, and it runs away from him, carrying his food and drink. He despairs of it, then comes to a tree and lies down in its shade, having given up hope of his mount. While he is in that state, he suddenly finds it standing before him. He takes hold of its rein and then, out of the intensity of his joy, says: 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord'—he made a mistake out of the intensity of his joy." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2747).]]

It is also established in the Sahih, through the narration of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, something similar to this. [[In manuscript T: "the same."]] [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2744).]]

Abd ar-Razzaq said, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of az-Zuhri, regarding His saying: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more delighted at the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his lost [[In manuscript T: "riding beast."]] in the place where he feared thirst would kill him." [[Tafsir Abd ar-Razzaq (2/156). It was also narrated with a connected chain, and Muslim transmitted it in his Sahih, no. (2675), through the route of Abd ar-Razzaq, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording.]]

Hammam ibn al-Harith said: Ibn Mas'ud was asked about a man who commits adultery with a woman and then marries her. He said: "There is no harm in it," and he recited: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, to the end of the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Sharik al-Qadi, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim an-Nakha'i, on the authority of Hammam, and mentioned it. [[Tafsir at-Tabari (25/18).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and pardons evil deeds﴾, meaning: He accepts repentance for the future and pardons evil deeds of the past. ﴿And He knows what you do﴾, meaning: He is aware of everything you have done, said and performed, and despite this He accepts the repentance of whoever turns to Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, as-Suddi said: this means He answers them. Ibn Jarir likewise said: its meaning is that He answers their supplication for themselves, for their companions and for their brothers. He related this from some of the grammarians (an-nuhat, i.e., Arabic grammarians), who considered it to be like His saying: ﴿So their Lord answered them﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 195].

Then he and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, from the hadith of al-A'mash, on the authority of Shaqiq ibn Salamah, on the authority of Salamah ibn Sabrah, who said: Mu'adh addressed us in Syria, saying: "You are the believers, and you are the people of Paradise. By Allah, I hope that Allah will admit into Paradise those of Persia and Byzantium whom you curse. That is because when one of you does a deed for another, he says: 'May Allah have mercy on you, you have done well, may Allah bless you, you have done well.'" Then he recited: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty﴾.

Ibn Jarir related from some people of Arabic (ahl al-'arabiyyah, i.e., grammarians) that he took His saying ﴿And He responds to those who believe﴾ to be like His saying: ﴿those who listen to the word﴾ [az-Zumar: 18], meaning: they are the ones who respond to the truth and follow it, like His saying, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Only those who listen will respond, and the dead—Allah will raise them﴾ [al-An'am: 36]. The first meaning is more apparent, because of His saying: ﴿and increases them from His bounty﴾, meaning: He answers their supplication and gives them beyond that. For this reason Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa narrated to us, saying: Baqiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abdullah al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, regarding His saying: ﴿and increases them from His bounty﴾: "It is intercession for one who deserves the Fire, from among those who did a kindness to them in this world." [[In manuscript T: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain from Abdullah."]] [[Abu Asim narrated it in as-Sunnah, no. (846), through the route of Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa, on the authority of Baqiyyah, and in its chain is Isma'il al-Kindi. adh-Dhahabi said in al-Mizan (1/235): "On the authority of al-A'mash, and from him Baqiyyah, with a strange and odd report."]]

Qatadah said, on the authority of Ibrahim an-Nakha'i al-Lakhmi, regarding His saying: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, he said: "They intercede for their brothers." ﴿And increases them from His bounty﴾, he said: "They intercede for the brothers of their brothers."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But the disbelievers will have a severe punishment﴾: when He mentioned the believers and the great reward they have, He mentioned the disbelievers and the severe punishment they have with Him on the Day of Resurrection, a painful and agonizing punishment on the day of their return and their reckoning.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If Allah were to expand provision for His servants, they would surely commit excess upon the earth﴾, meaning: if He gave them more than their need of provision, that would lead them to oppress and transgress against one another, out of arrogance and insolence.

Qatadah said: It used to be said: "The best of life is that which neither distracts you nor makes you transgress." Qatadah also mentioned the hadith: "I only fear for you what Allah brings forth of the splendour of the worldly life," and the questioner's question: "Can good bring forth evil?" [The hadith is cited in full.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But He sends down in measure what He wills. Indeed He is Acquainted and Seeing of His servants﴾, meaning: He provides them with what He chooses of provision, that in which their welfare lies, and He knows that best. So He makes rich whoever deserves riches and makes poor whoever deserves poverty. As came in the narrated hadith: "Among My servants there is one whom only wealth will set right; if I were to make him poor, I would corrupt his religion for him. And among My servants there is one whom only poverty will set right; if I were to make him rich, I would corrupt his religion for him."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired﴾, meaning: after people had given up hope of rain falling, He sends it down upon them at the time of their need and their dependence upon it, like His saying: ﴿And even though they had been, before it was sent down to them, in despair﴾ [ar-Rum: 49].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and spreads His mercy﴾, meaning: by it He encompasses existence for the people of that region and that area.

[[Narrated by at-Tabari in his tafsir (25/19).]]

The Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 42, verses 32–35:

He, exalted is He, says: Among His signs, which indicate His power and sovereignty, is that He subjected the sea so that ships run upon it by His command. The ships moving in the sea are like the *a'lam*, that is, like mountains. This is what Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said. That is, they are in the sea as mountains are on the land.

﴿If He wills, He stills the wind﴾, that is, the wind that propels the ships. Had He willed, He would have calmed it so that the ships would not move. Rather, they would remain motionless, neither coming nor going, but standing still on the surface of the water. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾, that is, steadfast in hardships, grateful. Indeed, in His subjecting the sea and causing the wind to blow in the measure they need for their journey, there are evidences of His favours upon His creatures. ﴿For every steadfast one﴾, that is, in hardships, ﴿grateful﴾ in ease.

* *

His saying: ﴿Or He wrecks them for what they have earned﴾, that is, had He willed, He would have destroyed the ships and drowned them because of the sins of their people who ride upon them. ﴿And He pardons much﴾, that is, of their sins. Had He seized them for all their sins, He would have destroyed everyone who rides the sea.

Some of the scholars of tafsir (exegesis) said: The meaning of His saying ﴿or He wrecks them for what they have earned﴾ is that had He willed, He would have sent a strong, violent wind which seized the ships and turned them from their straight course, driving them to the right or to the left, fleeing, not travelling on any path nor toward any destination.

This statement implies their destruction, and it is consistent with the first view, namely that had He willed, He would have stilled the wind so that the ships stopped, or strengthened it so that the ships scattered, fled and perished. But out of His gentleness and mercy, He sends it according to need, just as He sends rain in the amount that suffices. Had He sent it in great abundance, it would have demolished buildings; had He sent it in small amounts, it would not have made crops and fruits grow. Indeed, He sends it to lands like Egypt as flowing water (*sayh*) from another land, because they do not need rain. Had He sent rain upon them, it would have demolished their buildings and brought down their walls.

* *

His saying: ﴿And those who dispute concerning Our signs will know that they have no escape﴾, that is, they have no way of evading Our punishment and Our vengeance, for they are subdued by Our power.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 42, verses 36–39:

Allah, exalted is He, says, belittling the worldly life and its adornment, and what it contains of fleeting splendour and pleasure, saying: ﴿Whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾. That is: whatever you attain and gather, do not be deceived by it, for it is only the enjoyment of the worldly life, and it is a lowly, perishing abode that is inevitably transient. ﴿But what is with Allah is better and more lasting﴾. That is: the reward of Allah is better than the world, and it is everlasting and eternal. So do not prefer the perishing over the enduring. Hence He says: ﴿for those who have believed﴾, that is, for those who have been patient in abandoning the pleasures of this world, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, that is, so that He may help them to be patient in performing the obligations and avoiding the prohibitions.

Then He says: ﴿And those who avoid the major sins and immoralities﴾. We have already discussed sin (ithm) and immoralities (fawahish) in Surah al-A'raf. ﴿And when they are angered, they forgive﴾. That is: their disposition [and their nature and temperament] [[addition from A.]] requires pardon and forgiveness towards people; their disposition is not to take revenge on people.

It is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never took revenge for himself at all, except when the sacred limits of Allah were violated [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6126), from the hadith of 'A'ishah with the wording: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never took revenge for himself in anything, except when the sanctity of Allah was violated, then he would take revenge for Allah."]]. In another hadith: "When he was displeased with one of us [[in A: "with the man"]], he would say: 'What is the matter with him? May his forehead be dust-covered.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6031), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, [[in T: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain."]] from Ibrahim, who said: The believers used to dislike being humiliated, and when they were able [to retaliate], they would pardon.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who have responded to their Lord﴾, that is: they followed His messengers, obeyed His command and avoided His prohibitions. ﴿And established prayer﴾, which is the greatest of worship to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And their affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves﴾, that is: they do not finalise a matter until they consult about it, so that they assist one another with their opinions in matters such as war and what is similar to it, as Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And consult them in the matter; then when you have decided, rely upon Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 159]. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, used to consult them in wars and similar matters, to comfort their hearts thereby. Likewise, when 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was at the point of death after being stabbed, he made the matter after him a consultation among six men: 'Uthman, 'Ali, Talhah, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf (may Allah be pleased with them all). The opinion of all the Companions then converged on giving 'Uthman precedence over them (may Allah be pleased with them). ﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾, and this is by doing good to the creatures of Allah, beginning with those nearest to them, then those nearest after them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who, when tyranny afflicts them, they defend themselves﴾, that is: they have the strength to defend against those who wronged and transgressed against them; they are neither helpless nor humiliated, but are able to take revenge on whoever oppresses them. Yet even so, when they are able, they pardon, as Yusuf, peace be upon him, said to his brothers: ﴿No reproach will be upon you today. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3552. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it in al-Musannaf (10/347), and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (6/412) through the route of Abu al-Ahwas, and Ibn 'Adi said: "I do not know of anyone who narrates it from Abu Hamzah except Abu al-Ahwas."]

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the blame is only upon those who wrong people and oppress in the earth without right﴾, i.e., indeed the sin and the punishment are only upon them. i.e., they initiate people with injustice, as in the authentic hadith: "Those who revile one another, what they say falls upon the one who began, so long as the wronged one does not exceed the limit."

﴿Those — for them is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., severe and agonising.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Zayd, brother of Hammad ibn Zayd, narrated to us, 'Uthman al-Shahham narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Wasi', who said: "I came to Makkah and there was a watchtower over the trench, so I was seized and taken to Marwan ibn al-Muhallab, who was governor of Basra. He said: 'Your need, O Abu 'Abd Allah.' I said: 'My need is, if you can, to be like the one the brother of Banu 'Adi said.' He said: 'And who is the brother of Banu 'Adi?' He said: 'al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad, who once appointed a friend of his to a post, and he wrote to him: "As to what follows: if you can avoid spending the night except with a light back, an empty belly, and clean hands from the blood and wealth of the Muslims, then indeed when you do this, there will be no way against you. ﴿Indeed, the blame is only upon those who wrong people and oppress in the earth without right; those — for them is a painful punishment﴾."' Then Marwan said: 'He spoke the truth, by Allah, and gave sincere advice.' Then he said: 'What is your need, O Abu 'Abd Allah?' I said: 'My need is that you reunite me with my family.' He said: 'Yes.'" Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

[Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah (14/63).]

Then, when He condemned injustice and its people and legislated retaliation, He said, calling to pardon and forgiveness: ﴿But whoever is patient and forgives﴾, i.e., is patient over harm and conceals the evil deed, ﴿indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: [i.e.] [[Added from manuscript A: "i.e."]] it is among the matters of the right things that Allah commanded, i.e., among the praiseworthy matters and the commendable acts for which there is great reward and beautiful praise.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Imran ibn Musa al-Tarsusi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Samad ibn Yazid, servant of al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, narrated to us, who said: "I heard al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad say: [[Variant in manuscript T: "And from".]] When a man comes to you complaining to you about another man, say: 'O my brother, pardon him.' For pardon is closer to piety. If he says: 'My heart cannot bear pardon, but I will retaliate as my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded me,' then say to him [[Variant in manuscript T and A: "al-Fudayl said to him".]]: 'If you are skilled at retaliation, then do so; otherwise return to the door of pardon, for it is a wide door. Whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah. The one who pardons sleeps on his bed at night, while the one who retaliates turns over matters [in his mind].'" [[Followed in the original by: "Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya — meaning Ibn Sa'id al-Qattan — narrated to us, from Ibn 'Ajlan, who said: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id narrated to us, [[Variant in manuscript T: "And al-Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain".]] from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man reviled Abu Bakr while the Prophet ﷺ was sitting. The Prophet ﷺ began to marvel and smile. When the man went too far, Abu Bakr answered him with part of what he said. The Prophet ﷺ became angry and stood up. Abu Bakr followed him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, he was reviling me while you were sitting, but when I answered him with part of what he said, you became angry and stood up!" He said: "There was an angel with you, repelling him from you. When you answered him with part of what he said, the devil came [[Variant in manuscripts T, M and A: "occurred".]], and I would not sit with the devil." Then he said: "O Abu Bakr, there are three things, all of them true: No servant is wronged with an injustice and then overlooks it for the sake of Allah, except that Allah honours his support through it. No man opens a door of giving, seeking through it kinship, except that Allah increases him through it in abundance. And no man opens a door of begging, seeking through it increase, except that Allah increases him through it in poverty."

Abu Dawud similarly narrated it from 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, who said: and Safwan ibn 'Isa narrated it; both of them from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan. [[Al-Musnad (2/436) and Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. 4896, 4897.]] He narrated it also through the route of al-Layth, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Bashir ibn al-Muharrar, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, as a mursal report. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4897.]]

This hadith is extremely good in meaning, and it is the cause of its being related concerning al-Siddiq [[Variant in manuscripts T and A: "And this hadith is extremely good in meaning and fitting for al-Siddiq."; in manuscript M: "And this hadith is extremely good in meaning and fitting for al-Siddiq."]].

Ibn Kathir said, reporting about Himself, may He be exalted, that whatever He wills comes to be, and none can repel it; and whatever He does not will does not come to be, so there is no one to bring it into existence. Whomever He guides, none can lead astray; and whomever He leads astray, none can guide. As He said: ﴿And whoever He leads astray, you will not find for him any guiding ally﴾ [Al-Kahf: 17].

Then He said, reporting about the wrongdoers, who are the polytheists (mushrikun) who associate others with Allah: ﴿When they see the punishment﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, they will wish to return to the world, ﴿and say, "Is there any way to return?"﴾ As He said elsewhere: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and they say, "Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers." But rather, there has appeared to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars﴾ [Al-An'am: 27–28].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And you will see them exposed to it﴾, meaning the Fire, ﴿humbled by humiliation﴾, meaning the humiliation that has overtaken them because of their past disobedience to Allah, ﴿glancing with stealth﴾. Mujahid said: meaning in abasement. That is, they look at it furtively, out of fear of it. What they fear is certainly going to befall them, and it is greater than what is in their souls. May Allah protect us from that.

﴿And those who believed will say﴾, meaning they will say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning the greatest loss, as they are taken to the Fire, so they are deprived of their pleasure in the everlasting abode, they have lost themselves, and they are separated from their companions, their loved ones, their families and their relatives, so they have lost them. ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers will be in lasting punishment﴾, meaning constant, perpetual, everlasting, with no exit for them from it and no escape for them from it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And there will not be for them any allies to support them other than Allah﴾, meaning, to rescue them from the punishment and torment they are in. ﴿And whoever Allah sends astray, there is for him no path﴾, meaning there is for him no deliverance.
