When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned what will happen on the Day of Resurrection of terrors and great, awesome matters, He warned against it and commanded preparation for it, so He said: ﴿Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day that cannot be turned back by Allah﴾. That is, when He decrees its occurrence, it will happen in the blink of an eye, and there is no one to repel it or prevent it.

* *

His saying: ﴿You will have no refuge that Day, nor will you have any denial﴾ means: you will have no fortress to shelter in, nor any place to conceal you and let you hide from His sight, blessed and exalted is He. Rather, He encompasses you with His knowledge, His sight and His power, so there is no refuge from Him except in Him. ﴿On that Day man will say, "Where is the escape?" No! There is no refuge. To your Lord on that Day is the place of rest﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 10–12].

* *

His saying: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿then We have not sent you as a watcher over them﴾, that is: you are not a controller over them. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 272], and He said: ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 40], and here He said: ﴿Upon you is only the conveying﴾, that is: We have only charged you with conveying to them the message of Allah sent to them.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it﴾, that is: when prosperity and blessing befall him, he rejoices in that. ﴿And if an evil befalls them﴾, meaning the people, ﴿an evil﴾, that is: drought, calamity, affliction and hardship, ﴿then indeed man is ungrateful﴾, that is: he denies the blessings that came before and knows only the present moment. If a blessing reaches him, he becomes boastful and insolent, and if a trial reaches him, he despairs and becomes hopeless. As the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said [to the women]: "O women, give charity, for I have seen that most of the people of the Fire are you." A woman said: "Why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Because you complain often and you are ungrateful to your husbands. If you were good to one of them for a lifetime, and then something displeased her, she would say: 'I have never seen any good from you at all.'" [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 79, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), and no. 80, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).] This is the condition of most people, except those whom Allah guides and inspires with their right direction, and who are among those who believe and do righteous deeds. So the believer, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If good fortune befalls him, he gives thanks, and that is good for him; and if hardship befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him. And this is not for anyone except the believer." [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2999, from the hadith of Suhaib (may Allah be pleased with him).]

God Most High informs that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, their Owner, and the One who disposes of them. And that whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. And that He gives to whom He wills and withholds from whom He wills, and there is no one to prevent what He has given, and no one to give what He has withheld. And that He creates whatever He wills. And ﴿He bestows female [children] upon whom He wills﴾, meaning: He grants him only daughters. Al-Baghawi said: among them was Lot, peace be upon him. ﴿And He bestows male [children] upon whom He wills﴾, meaning: He grants him only sons. Al-Baghawi said: like Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him, to whom no daughter was born. ﴿Or He gives them both males and females﴾, meaning: He gives whomever He wills among people both a male and a female, i.e., from this and that [[In manuscript T: "this from this".]]. Al-Baghawi said: like Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. ﴿And He makes whom He wills barren﴾, meaning: he is not given offspring. Al-Baghawi said: like Yahya (John) and Isa (Jesus), peace be upon them both. Thus He made people into four categories: among them are those to whom He gives daughters, among them are those to whom He gives sons, among them are those to whom He gives both males and females, and among them are those whom He denies both, so He makes them barren, without offspring and without children. ﴿Indeed, He is All-Knowing﴾, meaning: of who deserves each of these categories. ﴿All-Powerful﴾, meaning: over whom He wills, regarding the variation among people in this.

This station resembles His statement about Isa: ﴿And that We may make him a sign for the people﴾ [Maryam: 21], meaning: a proof for them of His power, exalted and sanctified be He, in that He created creation in four categories. Adam, peace be upon him, was created from dust, neither from a male nor a female. Hawwa' (Eve), peace be upon her, was [created] [[Addition from manuscript T.]] from a male without a female. All the rest of creation, apart from Isa [peace be upon him] [[Addition from manuscripts T and M; in A: "Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon them both".]], is from a male and a female. And Isa, peace be upon him, is from a female without a male. Thus the proof was completed with the creation of Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon them both. Therefore He said: ﴿And that We may make him a sign for the people﴾. So this station concerns the parents, and the first station concerns the offspring, and each of them has four categories. Glory be to the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.

This is the states (maqamat) of revelation in relation to the majesty of Allah, may He be exalted, and it is that He, Exalted is He, sometimes casts into the heart (raw') of the Prophet ﷺ something about which there is no doubt that it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as came in Sahih Ibn Hibban, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Indeed the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) breathed into my heart: no soul will die until it has completed its provision and its term. So fear Allah and seek provision graciously."

[Narrated by al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah (14/304) through the chain of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Zubayd al-Yami, from one who informed him, from Ibn Mas'ud.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Or from behind a veil﴾ is like the speech of Musa, peace be upon him, for he asked to see Allah after the speech, and was denied that.

And in the Sahih, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Jabir ibn Abd Allah: "Allah has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil, but He spoke to your father face to face (kifahan)..." the hadith [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3010, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route."] Your father had been killed on the day of Uhud, but this is in the realm of the barzakh (intermediate state), whereas the verse refers to the abode of the worldly life.

* *

His saying: ﴿Or He sends a messenger and he reveals by His permission what He wills﴾ is like the sending down of Jibril [peace be upon him] and other angels upon the prophets, peace be upon them. ﴿Indeed He is Most High, All-Wise﴾, for He is Most High, All-Knowing, All-Aware, All-Wise.

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾, i.e., in the detail that has been prescribed for you in the Qur'an. ﴿But We made it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾, like His saying: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe a guidance and a healing; and as for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a far place﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed you, O Muhammad, guide to a straight path﴾, and it is the upright character (al-khuluq al-qawim). Then he explained it with His saying: ﴿The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, i.e., His law which Allah commanded, ﴿to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, i.e., their Lord and their Owner, and the One who disposes of them, the Ruler whose judgment none can repel. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah do all matters return﴾, i.e., affairs return to Him, and He decides them and judges concerning them.

And in the Sahih, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Jabir ibn Abd Allah: "Allah has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil, but He spoke to your father face to face (kifahan)..." the hadith [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3010, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route."] Your father had been killed on the day of Uhud, but this is in the realm of the barzakh (intermediate state), whereas the verse refers to the abode of the worldly life.

* *

His saying: ﴿Or He sends a messenger and he reveals by His permission what He wills﴾ is like the sending down of Jibril [peace be upon him] and other angels upon the prophets, peace be upon them. ﴿Indeed He is Most High, All-Wise﴾, for He is Most High, All-Knowing, All-Aware, All-Wise.

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾, i.e., in the detail that has been prescribed for you in the Qur'an. ﴿But We made it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾, like His saying: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe a guidance and a healing; and as for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a far place﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed you, O Muhammad, guide to a straight path﴾, and it is the upright character (al-khuluq al-qawim). Then he explained it with His saying: ﴿The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, i.e., His law which Allah commanded, ﴿to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, i.e., their Lord and their Owner, and the One who disposes of them, the Ruler whose judgment none can repel. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah do all matters return﴾, i.e., affairs return to Him, and He decides them and judges concerning them.

End of the tafsir of Surah "Ha Mim" al-Shura, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

This is the states (maqamat) of revelation in relation to the majesty of Allah, may He be exalted, and it is that He, Exalted is He, sometimes casts into the heart (raw') of the Prophet ﷺ something about which there is no doubt that it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as came in Sahih Ibn Hibban, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Indeed the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) breathed into my heart: no soul will die until it has completed its provision and its term. So fear Allah and seek provision graciously."

[Narrated by al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah (14/304) through the chain of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Zubayd al-Yami, from one who informed him, from Ibn Mas'ud.]
